learning_outcomes.text: Students can structure, create, and fundamentally control a project using professional project management software. They apply their project management know-how using a continuous, practical case study to independently develop problem solutions. In particular, they are familiar with handling disruptions in the project process and have practiced it using examples.

Students design and implement their own viable concepts for the following central topics of project management: meeting management, workshop organization and moderation, communication management, risk management, and project controlling. The appropriate methods and techniques have been practiced through case studies and are familiar.

syllabus_topics: Creating Project and Work Breakdown Structure (WBS, PSP)
Creating resources and preparing a resource-loaded schedule
The baseline and the contractor's schedule
Project disruption and integration of the contractor's schedule
Meeting management, workshop organization and workshop moderation
teaching_methods: hybrid practical seminar in the computer lab
assessment_rules: To receive credit points, the module examination must be passed. The specific assessment method (exam, oral examination, or written assignment with presentation) will be determined at the beginning of the lecture. The grade weighting for the final grade is based on credit points.
bibliography: Harris: Planning and Control Using Oracle Primavera P6
